title: Milky Way and star trails over ALMA
caption: The Milky Way and star trails over ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Star trails run through the sky above the ALMA Observatory while the depth of the Milky Way glows behind them. At the center of the picture sits a darker spot, the Coalsack Nebula, which lies in Crux, the constellation better known as the Southern Cross.

This long-exposure photograph shows two things at once. The rich band of our galaxy reveals how deep and crowded the Milky Way is, while the trails reveal Earth's rotation. As the planet turns, the camera turns with it, so each star is drawn out into an arc.

The Coalsack is a dark nebula, a dense cloud of dust that blocks the light of the stars behind it. Against the bright background of the Milky Way, it shows up as a shadowy patch. Many dark nebulae are only noticeable because of that contrast, standing out as holes in the starlight rather than glowing on their own.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at ALMA. The exposure settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points and the Milky Way as a faint band. The long exposure turns the stars into trails and brightens the galaxy's glow.

explore: ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, observes at wavelengths far longer than visible light, which lets it study cold dust clouds like those that make up dark nebulae.
alt: Star trails over the ALMA Observatory, with the Milky Way behind them and a dark patch at the center of the sky.
